words.prose: {{ar:لَآ}} ({{tr:la}}) launches the clause as negated classification, not as a denied finite action. It negates the relation {{ar:أَنتُمْ عَٰبِدُونَ}} ({{tr:antum abiduna}}), so the addressees are excluded from the worshipper class defined by the speaker's object. The embedded {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:a'budu}}) is not negated; it remains the positive act that specifies what the addressees are not worshippers of. The long particle also returns the refrain of 109:2-5, making negation the first semantic pressure after the connector.

words.prose: {{ar:أَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:antum}}) makes the addressed group explicit before the predicate arrives. The denial is therefore not anonymous or merely inferred from verb morphology: the plural addressees stand in the foreground, and {{ar:عَٰبِدُونَ}} ({{tr:abiduna}}) is then attached to them as the denied classification. Across the boundary from 109:4, the center of attention flips from the speaker's explicit self-reference to the addressees, while the speaker returns only inside the embedded verb {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:a'budu}}).

words.prose: {{ar:عَٰبِدُونَ}} ({{tr:abiduna}}) is the predicate placed on {{ar:أَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:antum}}), so the denial lands as collective identity: the addressees are not worshippers of {{ar:مَآ أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:ma a'budu}}). The active participle still governs its object phrase, so the claim is not a general denial that they worship anything; it excludes them from the worshipper class defined by the speaker's worship. The root {{ar:ع ب د}} ({{tr:ʿ-b-d}}) adds servitude, practiced submission, and path-like tractability pressure: the denied identity is not a bare title or belief label, but a shaped devotional orientation. Local grammar keeps that pressure inside worshipper identity rather than turning the word into an independent road, taming, or enslavement claim. Its plural ending reverses the prior singular participle from 109:4, and its return from the 109:3 refrain makes a marked identity-form carry the same root again as a collective predicate before the final verb changes that root into the speaker's ongoing action.

topics.headline: servitude and path pressure thicken worshipper identity
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the denied worshipper identity as devoted service and shaped submission, while the local participle keeps it from becoming an unrelated road or enslavement claim.
topics.reason: V4 supports worship and submissive obedience within {{ar:ع ب د}} ({{tr:ʿ-b-d}}), and also records slave-status and smoothed-road branches, but the local active participle selects worshipper or servant identity rather than those non-surface branches as independent senses.

words.prose: {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:ma}}) supplies the object domain for {{ar:عَٰبِدُونَ}} ({{tr:abiduna}}), but it does so by pointing forward into {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:a'budu}}) instead of naming the object directly. The main parse is relative: the addressees are not worshippers of that which the speaker worships. Because the same surface can also press toward a verbal-noun reading, the phrase can carry a second pressure, the mode or act of worship, but that remains nested inside the local relative-clause structure. Its long open sound gives the unnamed object or mode audible space before the final verb defines it, and its repetition across the surah keeps the objects unnamed while the persons and tenses alternate.

topics.headline: unnamed object also leaves mode pressure

words.prose: {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:a'budu}}) closes the ayah by completing the relative clause of {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:ma}}); the main denial is fully specified only when this final verb arrives. Its first-person subject is carried by the prefix rather than by a separate pronoun, so the addressees remain foregrounded in {{ar:أَنتُمْ}} ({{tr:antum}}) while the speaker's agency is embedded in the worship verb. As an imperfect, it keeps the speaker's worship ongoing after the past-tense contrast of 109:4. The verb is object-linked through {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:ma}}), yet its bare shape without an object suffix leaves that marker as the visible object head, keeps the referent unnamed, and lets the act feel like a standing orientation of worshipful service. The root {{ar:ع ب د}} ({{tr:ʿ-b-d}}) supplies obedience, servitude, and repeated path-making pressure, so the imperfect sounds like continuous service that treads and maintains a way rather than a one-time ritual or thin belief label. Local Form I still selects the speaker's devoted service rather than causative enslavement. At the ending, the same root that named the addressees' denied identity in {{ar:عَٰبِدُونَ}} ({{tr:abiduna}}) becomes the speaker's ongoing act, repeating the 109:3 closing phrase and preparing for the final religious-allocation formula in 109:6.

topics.headline: first-person agency is embedded in the verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the speaker is present as worshipping agent, but only inside the verb after the addressees have been foregrounded.
topics.reason: QAC identifies {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:a'budu}}) as first-person singular imperfect, and attachment evidence says its subject is syntactically controlled by the quoted speaker.

topics.headline: imperfect aspect answers the prior past
topics.reader_payoff: The reader feels the boundary move from completed addressee worship in 109:4 into the speaker's ongoing worship at the close of 109:5.
topics.reason: The local form is an imperfect first-person verb, and the source rows contrast it with the past second-person verb in 109:4.

topics.headline: directed worship still feels like whole orientation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees that the worship is directed through the relative object, while the bare verb still carries the feel of a standing act of devotion.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence supplies {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:ma}}) as the explicit object link, while the verb has no object suffix; contextual valency shows object-linked usage is dominant but not exclusive.

topics.headline: final verb positively defines the object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader waits until the last word to know the object relation that defines the addressees' denied predicate.
topics.reason: {{ar:أَعْبُدُ}} ({{tr:a'budu}}) completes the relative clause of {{ar:مَآ}} ({{tr:ma}}) and is not itself governed by the main negation.

topics.headline: obedient service thickens the imperfect verb
topics.reader_payoff: The reader hears ongoing worship as obedient service and maintained orientation, while local Form I blocks causative enslavement as the selected sense.
topics.reason: V4 supports worship and submissive obedience for {{ar:ع ب د}} ({{tr:ʿ-b-d}}), but the local Form I imperfect is the speaker's service or worship, not Form II or Form X causation imposed on another.

topics.headline: same root shifts from identity to action

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The negated predicate عَٰبِدُونَ at word 3 is a plural agent noun, while أَعْبُدُ at word 5 is a first-person verb governed through مَا.
baseline_models.mechanism: The shared worship-and-submissive-obedience branch binds the two tokens, but the noun–verb asymmetry separates an inhabited servant identity from an enacted service. The negation therefore denies congruence between the addressees' settled posture and the speaker's directed act, not merely simultaneous performance of different rites.

activation_trace.role: Submissive worship supplies the common relation whose nominal agent-state and verbal enactment are held apart.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The same ع ب د root predicates a status of the addressees and names the speaker's action toward مَا.
baseline_models.mechanism: The root's owned-status, enslavement, and honoring branches make worship a vertical social relation: one belongs, is subdued, serves, and magnifies. The verse can thus deny a shared mastery relation rather than only a shared cultic object; the parties are not interchangeable occupants of one economy of owner, servant, and honored claimant.

activation_trace.role: Owned servant-status turns عَٰبِدُونَ into a relation of belonging, not only a label for ritual performers.
The causative image of reducing someone to servitude exposes the power relation implicit in directed service.
Honoring and magnifying identifies the served object as the claimant elevated by the act.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: عَٰبِدُونَ and أَعْبُدُ repeat one root across the agent and the act, with مَا marking the act's orientation.

The negation can therefore picture the addressees' formed route as not running toward what the speaker's service opens toward.

strongest_changes: The focus-only noun–verb asymmetry changes a flat denial of shared ritual into a distinction between settled servant identity and directed act.
The speech cue makes the line a public boundary act, and the verb/noun/perfect sequence makes its exact return a closure across action, identity, and prior practice.
The final د ي ن branches widen worship into separate habitual orders of obedience, while ownership and debt sustain a coexisting legal-social model of nontransferable claims.
summary.what_was_special: One repeated root carries worship, servant-status, enslavement, honor, and road-making, while ordered context turns an apparently redundant line into performative and temporal closure. The packet's split and cross-domain branches also preserve live independence, submission-overlap, obligation, and jurisdiction readings without forcing them into one interpretation.
remaining_uncertainties: The packet does not settle whether مَا should be heard chiefly as object, content, or a broader orientation of worship.
The exact temporal force assigned to nominal, present-verbal, and perfect forms may be less exhaustive than the sequence model proposes.
The non-dominant ق ل ل echo and the debt and city activations may be productive abductive resonances or merely branch-distance effects.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Exact repetition turns relational denial into closure.** The fixed ayah again supplies ع ب د B003 through عَٰبِدُونَ and أَعْبُدُ. The structural activator is its exact match with 109:3 after the intervening 109:4. Mechanism: the repeated line closes the loop: even after the speaker's own identity has been protected from their past practice, the addressees remain non-participants in the speaker's worship-relation. The abductive move is mine: the packet gives exact repetition; I infer closure from return-after-interruption. Reading change: 109:5 reads as sealing, not redundancy.

2. **The addressees are not servants in the speaker's honoring order.** ع ب د B006, "honoring and magnifying," is activated by the same مَا أَعْبُدُ object and by the basmalah's named divine frame. Mechanism: the repeated plural participle denies not only ritual performance but a service/honor orientation. The abductive move is mine: the packet gives honor/service and repeated object orientation; I infer that repetition confirms a stable honor mismatch. Reading change: the ayah says that the speaker's object of worship is not merely unchosen by them but not honored by them in the required mode.

3. **Resistance to scattering becomes stronger after repetition.** ع ب د B010, "scattering in different directions," is activated by the plural and by the copied 109:3 structure. Mechanism: the exact repetition gathers possible scattered divergences into one formal statement; individual variations do not matter for the packet's declared boundary. The abductive move is mine: the packet gives the scattering branch; I infer that duplicated syntax suppresses dispersion. Reading change: 109:5 reads as a second clamp on the group-level boundary.

4. **The ayah prepares the final legal/accounting allotment.** ع ب د B001, "slavery and owned status," and B004, "making someone a slave," are activated by د ي ن B004 in 109:6. Mechanism: by denying that the addressees are worshippers of what the speaker worships, the ayah prevents their being counted as belonging to the speaker's obedience/order. The abductive move is mine: the packet gives servile status under ع ب د and subjugation/possession under د ي ن; I infer that final allotment depends on non-ownership/non-belonging. Reading change: the repeated denial becomes preparatory sorting for لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ وَلِىَ دِينِ.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: The final ayah, when reread backward, made 109:5 feel immediately transitional. At first it could look like duplication of 109:3, but 109:6 shows why it returns: the repeated denial is the last sorting act before dīn is distributed by pronoun. The intervening 109:4 also made the repetition non-redundant, because the addressees' role-denial is restated after the speaker has refused relation to their past worship. This strengthened ع ب د B001/B004 as status-protection: no party is counted as belonging to the other's worship-order.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **Exact recurrence closes the reciprocal test.** The fixed clause repeats 109:3 word for word, again grounding both sides in `ع ب د B003`. Between the two occurrences, 109:4 tests the reverse relation with the speaker as participial servant and the addressees’ service in the perfect. The second occurrence is assigned the role of restoring the first orientation after that reversal. I infer from exact recurrence that neither direction of assimilation has survived the test. The line therefore functions as closure, not redundant restatement.

2. **The repeated participle stabilizes a role/object mismatch.** Fixed **أَنتُمْ عَٰبِدُونَ** is a nominal predication, while **أَعْبُدُ** remains verbal; repetition now adds textual duration to that grammatical contrast. `ع ب د B003` supplies submissive service, and `ع ب د B006` supplies the honor accorded to what is served. The addressees’ role is structurally held apart from the speaker’s continuing object-relation. I infer that a role repeated unchanged across the intervening reverse clause is being presented as stable. The reading shifts from failure to perform one act to an enduring mismatch in allegiance and recognition.

3. **The service relation opens into divergent routes.** Exploratorily, fixed **عبد** can activate `ع ب د B010`, whose accepted image is groups or routes scattering in different directions. Its direct forms are more remote from **عَٰبِدُونَ**, so the branch is retained only because 109:6 immediately partitions **دِين** with **لَكُمْ / وَلِيَ**, while 109:3–5 have already separated service objects. The branch supplies spatial divergence; I infer the arrow that different service objects generate different ways. The fixed denial can thus be read as the final point at which the two routes cease to coincide before they are named as separate **دِين**.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 109:6 was the decisive later activator. Its immediate **لَكُمْ / وَلِيَ** partition changed the repeated clause from a backward-looking echo into the threshold of explicit allocation, and it supplied the directional mechanism needed for the exploratory `ع ب د B010` image of diverging routes. Its `د ي ن B001/B005` branches also confirmed that the stabilized mismatch concerns organized, customary allegiance rather than one omitted act.

findings.text: 109:3'ün aynen dönmesi, aradaki ters yönlü sınamadan sonra iki yöndeki ibadet özdeşleşmesinin de kapanmış olduğunu mühürler.
Tekrarlanan isim biçimi, muhatapların rolü ile konuşanın sürekli kulluk yönelimi arasındaki değer verme ve bağlılık uyuşmazlığını kalıcılaştırır.
Son ayrım öncesindeki bu tekrar, hiçbir tarafın ötekinin kulluk düzenine ait veya onun sahipliği altında sayılmamasını sağlayan son tasnif işlevi görür.
Farklı kulluk nesnelerinin iki yolu birbirinden ayırdığı okuması, dağılma çağrışımının doğrudan olmayan kullanımına dayandığından spekülatiftir.
Tekrarlanan çoğul yapının muhataplar arasındaki bütün dağınık istisnaları kapattığı okuması da aynı uzak çağrışımı dil bilgisel kesinliğe dönüştürdüğü için spekülatiftir.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Crowned Voice and Honored Ruler
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A titled ruler is crowned, speaks with social force, and receives honor and service.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: effective local ruler (`ق و ل:B004/m01`); titled woman (`ق و ل:B004/m02`); crown (`ك ف ر:B015/m01`); coronation (`ك ف ر:B015/m02`); honored or served superior (`ع ب د:B006/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The ruler motif supplies the speaking office, coronation marks that office visibly, and the honored superior completes the hierarchy through received service. The feminine title preserves the same ranked social role with a different bearer.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Bowed Service and Devotional Allegiance
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Worship is enacted as directed service, with bodily lowering expressing the worshipper's chosen allegiance.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: devotional worship (`ع ب د:B003/m01`); bowed salute with lowered head or hand to chest (`ك ف ر:B014/m01`)
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The repeated worship relation acquires a bodily counterpart in the bowed salute. Action and posture together form a scene of allegiance rather than a merely abstract profession.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Chattel Hierarchy and Coerced Labor
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: Dominion reduces a person to owned status and compels work under humiliating control.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: chattel slave (`ع ب د:B001/m01`); saleable human property (`ع ب د:B001/m02`); making someone a slave (`ع ب د:B004/m01`); coercing slave-like labor (`ع ب د:B004/m02`); humiliating compulsion (`د ي ن:B004/m01`); dominion and ownership (`د ي ن:B004/m02`)

The scene turns the vocabulary of service into a complete hierarchy of possessor, possessed person, compulsion, and work.
